title: soft-slowpath-retry-mitigation-and-local-circuit-preservation
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Hotfix: Reduce cascading circuit opens caused by client retry storms. Adds retry attribution, bounded slowpath requeue with exponential backoff, and circuit hysteresis to improve SLO stability.
description:
Context: During a transient backend slowdown (root cause in external datastore), client libraries with aggressive retries amplified tail latency and generated a burst of slowpath requests. The SLO enforcer counted the resulting error/timeouts and flipped a number of region-local circuit breakers aggressively. Those circuit transitions in turn triggered reroutes and client retries, causing a short-lived cascade that violated regional latency SLOs and increased error budget burn.

Motivation: We need a minimal-risk, fast-path hotfix that reduces retry amplification and preserves local circuit state long enough for transient backpressure to recover. The change aims to (1) prevent retries from being double-counted in SLO-driven circuit opens, (2) avoid unbounded requeueing into the slowpath queue, and (3) add hysteresis to local circuit transitions so transient spikes do not immediately flip a circuit to open.

What this PR does (single-continuous description): Adds a "retry_guard" layer that tags requests coming from client retries and instructs the SLO enforcer to attribute retry attempts separately from original submissions; introduces a bounded, time-to-live slowpath requeue (configurable: slo.slowpath.requeue.max=200, slo.slowpath.requeue.ttl=30s) with exponential backoff and jitter to prevent thundering re-enqueue loops; implements a local-circuit hysteresis window (configurable: circuit.hysteresis.window=45s) and a soften-open state where circuits move to "degraded" before fully "open" to allow steady-state recovery; updates the enforcer to use a sliding-window error attribution that subtracts traced retry-attempts from the base error counts used for immediate circuit decisions. Adds lightweight metrics (retry_guard.attempts, slowpath.requeues, circuit.hysteresis_transitions) and a small observability dashboard patch.

Files and areas changed (high-level): runtime/slo/enforcer.go (retry attribution and sliding-window logic), runtime/circuit/manager.go (hysteresis state machine and metrics), runtime/queue/slowpath_requeue.go (bounded requeue implementation + backoff), controlplane/config/flags.go (feature flags and defaults), ci/canary/perf_canary.yaml (canary job adjustments), docs/observability/slo-runbooks.md (runbook additions), deploy/helm/templates/configmap.yaml (new config knobs).

Testing and validation: Unit tests for the retry attribution and hysteresis state machine added (enforcer_test.go, circuit_manager_test.go). Integration test simulating retry storms added to perf-canary suite. Canary run (us-west-2) for 6 hours against a synthetic slowpath workload: median p95 latency dropped by 9%, SLO error budget burn reduced by ~63% during the injected slowdown window. Load tests verified bounded requeue memory usage (peak requeue queue depth <= 200 as configured).

Rollout plan: squash-merge to main, gated by feature flag slo.retry_guard.enabled (default: true for hotfix). Staged deployment: canary to us-west-2 -> us-east -> eu-central with health checks for p95 and error-budget. If any region shows >5% SLO regression post-rollout, the feature flag can be toggled off immediately; the PR includes a quick disable path.

Backward compatibility: All new behavior is behind config/flag knobs and uses conservative defaults suitable for immediate enabling. No protocol or API changes.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration canary test added
- [x] Metrics and dashboards updated
- [x] Docs runbook updated
- [x] Config knobs added for rapid rollback

Related tickets: ENG-18204 (primary), SRE-491 (incident), INT-5593 (customer impacted case).
